newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore leaders threaten to sue poll candidate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore leaders threaten to sue poll candidate.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and six others of the ruling party have threatened to sue an opposition candidate for libel and slander, the Straits Times reported on Wednesday.

Letters have been sent to Workers' Party (WP) candidate for parliament Tang Liang Hong saying he had gravely slandered and libelled the members of the People's Action Party (PAP) in an interview published on Tuesday, the newspaper said.
Singapore holds parliamentary elections on Thursday.
Tang was advised in the letters from PAP lawyers that if he did not withdraw his remarks and apologise for them by 9 p.m. (1300 GMT) on Wednesday, legal action would be taken against him.
PAP leaders have accused Tang of harbouring anti-Christian and communal Chinese views in a society that witnessed race riots in the 1960s.
Tang said in the interview that PAP leaders had concocted lies and defamed him.

The Straits Times reported that at a rally late on Tuesday night, Goh said of the interview: "It is a very serious thing...because if he is right and I am a liar, I should step down immediately as Prime Minister."

"You cannot have a cheat and a liar as the prime minister. So, immediately, we sent out a letter to him today, with a writ all ready, asking him to apologise. If he doesn't, then legal action will proceed, he will be sued."
No one was immediately available in Goh's and Lee's offices or the WP office to comment on the reports.
Tang had himself said earlier he would sue Lee, Goh and other PAP members over charges they have made against him.
But he is yet to follow through on his threats of legal action, saying he was too busy campaigning ahead of the election.
